message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (including streaming releases). I’ve grouped them by release platform and added a short note on why each one stands out.

| Platform | Film | Why it’s worth watching |
|----------|------|------------------------|
| **Theatrical** | **“The Little Things” (2021)** – *Note: Released in late 2020 in some markets* | A gritty, atmospheric mystery starring Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, and Jared Leto. It blends procedural elements with psychological tension, and the performances keep you guessing until the end. |
| | **“The Hunt” (2020)** | A tense thriller about a man who becomes the target of a violent mob hunt after being falsely accused. It’s a stark look at paranoia and mob mentality, with strong direction and a solid cast. |
| | **“The Nightingale” (2020)** | Though more historical drama, its crime‑thriller core—revenge, survival, and moral ambiguity—makes it a compelling watch. The film’s pacing and character focus create a tense atmosphere. |
| | **“The Invisible Man” (2020)** | A modern retelling of the classic horror story, but with a strong crime‑thriller edge. It’s a smart, suspenseful film that explores abuse, gaslighting, and the fear of unseen threats. |
| | **“The Last Full Measure” (2020)** | A war‑drama with crime‑thriller undertones, focusing on a soldier’s quest for justice. The investigative narrative and moral questions give it a thriller feel. |
| | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7” (2020)** | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller. Its real‑world stakes and sharp dialogue make it a gripping watch. |
| | **“The Last Duel” (2021)** | Released in 2021 but premiered in 2020 festivals; a historical crime‑thriller that examines truth, justice, and gender dynamics. |
